Exam Date & Time: 20-Jan-2023 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
 THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. (COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING) EXAMINATIONS -  
  JANUARY/FEBRUARY 2023  
  SUBJECT : CSE 2151 - COMPUTER ORGANIZATION AND ARCHITECTURE  
  (MAKEUP)  
  COMPUTER ORGANIZATION AND ARCHITECTURE [CSE 2151]  
Marks: 50                                                                               Duration: 180 mins.  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
1A)          Assume that an array A is stored in consecutive word locations starting from address A  
  and an array B is stored in consecutive word locations starting from address B. Write a  
  CISC-style program to find the product of the corresponding elements of two arrays and  
  store it in the third array C starting at address C. Assume uniform sized arrays with the (3)  
  size of the array stored in memory location SIZE. Assume byte addressable memory and  
  word length is two bytes.  
  
1B)           Represent the following integers in 2's complement representation with minimum  
  number of bits required, perform the operation mentioned and state whether overflow  
  occurs or not in each case. Also, if overflow has occurred, state why it has occurred.   (3)  
  i) Add -8 with -7  
  ii) Subtract +15 from -16  
  
$$1C)           Consider two decimal numbers A= +81.375 B= +15.5$$  
  Perform the following operations:  
  a) Convert the decimal numbers to floating point binary  
  b) Normalize the number obtained above in (a)  
  c) Represent the normalized numbers in IEEE32 bit floating point representation          (4)  
  d) Perform (A / B), on the numbers represented in (c) using the rules for division of  
  IEEE 32 bit floating point representation. Indicate all the steps clearly  
  e) Store the result in the IEEE 32-bit floating-point representation  
  
2A)           Considering 1010 as Dividend and 0011 as Divisor, perform the division using restoring  
  division algorithm.                                                                    (3)  
  
2B)           Depict the Hardware Implementation of Multiplication of unsigned Binary Numbers.  
  (2)  
  
2C)           In context of the hardwired control unit design, draw the state diagram of the Booth's  
  Multiplier Controller along with the steps in its controller action. In what ways, the  
  Hardwired Control Design Mechanism is disadvantageous in comparison with that of         (5)  
  the Microprogrammed Control Unit Design Mechanisms.  
  
3A)           Design a Microprogrammed control unit using Wilke's design for the Register Transfer     (3)  
  Description given below:

3B)   A computer has a small data cache capable of holding eight words and has a byte  
  addressable memory. Each cache block consists of one word and one word comprises of  
  one byte. When a given program is executed, the processor reads data sequentially from  
  the addresses given below (Addresses are given in decimal). Assume that the cache is  
  initially empty. Show the contents of the cache after each memory access, for a Direct (5)  
  mapped cache, and compute the hit rate  
  7200, 7201, 7208, 7213, 7200, 7216, 7208, 7201, 7215, 7201, 7213, 7218, 7220, 7213,  
  7217, 7219  
  
3C)   A disk unit has 25 recording surfaces. It has a total of 16,000 cylinders. There is an  
  average of 200 sectors per track. Each sector contains 512 bytes of data. What is the  
  maximum number of bytes that can be stored in this unit? What is the data transfer rate    (2)  
  in bytes per second at a rotational speed of 7200 rpm?  
  
4A)   Design a large memory consisting of 4G words of 64 bits each for a system. There are 2  
  types of static memory chips available of same physical size, 512M × 8 and 1024M ×  
  16. Identify the most suitable memory chip such that a smaller decoder is used and       (3)  
  justify the answer. Draw the structure and indicate clearly, the number of address lines  
  and the data lines for large memory chips in the diagram.  
  
4B)   A computer has a data cache capable of holding 16 words and each word is one byte.  
  The cache block consists of two words and initially the cache is empty. When the  
  program is executed, the processor reads the data from the following decimal addresses  
  given below. The data is stored in continuous location of the main memory starting from  
  location 1000 to 1031. Show the organization of the words in the main memory.           (5)  
  Compare and identify the most suitable mapping technique to solve this problem. Show  
  the contents of cache using each technique. If blocks are grouped into sets, then a  
  maximum of 2 blocks can be grouped into a single set.  
  1000, 1003, 1004, 1007, 1009, 1010, 1012, 1015  
  
4C)   Distinguish between UMA and NUMA multiprocessor as far as network latency is  
  concerned.                                                                                 (2)  
  
5A)   The Informatics Business unit of Delta Information Solutions, a Multinational Company  
  operates on shared memory multiprocessors which demands an interconnection that  
  requires a direct link between any pair of units connected to the network to connect its  
  primary constituent units namely the FinTech Group, the Technology Solutions Group,  
  Business Solutions Group, Technology Analytics Group and Market Research Group.          (5)  
  Assume, each of these groups is an independent processing unit. Identify the type of  
  interconnection network and explain its structure diagrammatically. Discuss the Ring  
  Based Interconnection Networks along with the hierarchy of rings.  
  
5B)   Give the diagrammatic depiction of the five-stage pipelining architecture and enlist the   (3)  
  significance of the various interstage buffers in the architecture drawn.

5C)             Distinguish between Fine-Grained Multithreading and Coarse-Grained Multithreading.  
  (2)
